about_the_game:
Metro City, 1999. Follow leather-jacket-wearing, chain-smoking, no-nonsense detective Jason Maxx as he investigates a man who mysteriously fell to his death.

Things, however, might get a little goofy.

Metro City is an absurd place full of silly characters, sight gags and low poly, retro 3D graphics. Sarcastic quips, visual humor and low-res textures abound!

Solve the mystery through a series of conversations, interrogations, combing of clues and the occasional meeting with a murderous maniac.

Get the clues, meet some weirdos and solve the case!

Features:

  • Play as a hardcore 90’s noir detective

  • Fun conversations with oddball characters

  • Explore the dark eerie Metro City

  • 1-2 hour playthrough

  • Dark humor aplenty!

content_descriptors.notes:
Sex & Nudity: Mild

Very brief sex-related jokes.

Violence & Gore: Moderate

Some blood, shooting and police-related action. A corpse is seen, with no graphic gore.

Profanity: Severe

Several uses of the words “b!tch”, “d@mn”, “sh!t”, “@ss”, “pu$$y”. Few but multiple uses of the word “f#ck”.

Alcohol, Drugs & Smoking: Moderate

Some characters smoke and purchase cigarettes. There are several tongue-in-cheek comments about cigarette, alcohol and drug use.

Frightening & Intense Content: Moderate

There’s very dark humor throughout. There are jokes about suicide, murder, organized crime, mental health, death of family members, violence towards children, violence towards animals, evil corporations, gun use, police corruption and prostitution. A corpse is seen. The tone of the game is dark and atmospheric, but the dialogue is often very comedic and the characters often behave in silly ways. The game is rather self-aware and satirical; it doesn’t wallow in the darkness.

short_description: A man has fallen to his death in Metro City. Mysterious circumstances. Luckily, edgy 90’s detective Jason Maxx is on the case. The city is dark, the suspects are zany, and the graphics are Y2K-crusty. Explore, interrogate. Can Jason solve the mystery, even when absurdity takes over?
